puzzles.title: Mummy TD
puzzles.question: What are the odds? (%)
puzzles.solution: Blitz in Mummy, do not rr BD results. If not to knock down or push away - 4++ dodge
puzzles.author: WorldSitar, Akyama & neproxy, Rubbl Final

puzzles.title: The Loose Ball
puzzles.imageAlt: Pitch diagram: Blitzer next to a loose ball held in one tackle zone
puzzles.task:
Turn 8 of the second half and you are one touchdown behind. The ball is loose one square inside the opponent's half, right next to your **Blitzer #1**. The bad news: the ball lies in the tackle zone of the opposing Lineman #5.

Your Blitzer has to pick the ball up (**4+**: AG 3+ with -1 for the tackle zone), then he just has to walk 4 open squares into the end zone. He has **Sure Hands** and you have **no Team Re-Roll** left this turn.
puzzles.question: What is the chance that you score the touchdown this turn? (%)
puzzles.solution:
**Step 1 - pick the ball up.** AG 3+ with one opposing tackle zone is a **4+** roll: 3 faces out of 6, so exactly 50%.

**Step 2 - Sure Hands.** Sure Hands re-rolls a failed pick-up, so the ball comes up once in 1 - (1/2)² = 1 - 1/4 = **3/4 = 75%** of the cases.

- Pick-up on the first try: 50%
- Pick-up on the Sure Hands re-roll: the other 50% x 50% = 25%
- Everything else: the ball stays loose - turnover

**Step 3 - the run.** Four open squares, no dodge, no rush, no opponent in reach: automatic (0 re-rolls needed).

Total: 75% x 100% = **75%**.

This is why Sure Hands is the single most annoying skill in the game for a defence.
puzzles.author: demo

puzzles.title: Quick Pass, Clean Catch
puzzles.imageAlt: Pitch diagram: thrower in the open passing to a catcher in the end zone
puzzles.task:
Turn 16, and you are two squares short of the draw. **#3 Thrower** stands in the open with the ball, **#4 Catcher** is already standing in the end zone. Nobody is marking the thrower and nobody is marking the catcher.

The pass is a **Quick Pass: 2+** (PA 2+, no modifiers). The catch is a **3+** for the Catcher (AG 3+, no modifiers) and he has the **Catch** skill. You have no Team Re-Roll left.
puzzles.question: What is the chance of a completed pass and a touchdown? (%)
puzzles.solution:
The two rolls are independent, so the chances multiply.

**Pass (2+):** 5 success faces out of 6 = 5/6 = 83.33%.

**Catch (3+ with Catch):** a 3+ is 4/6 = 2/3 = 66.67%; Catch re-rolls the failure, so 1 - (1/3)² = 8/9 = 88.89%.

Total: 5/6 x 8/9 = 40/54 = **74.07%**, which rounds to **74%**.

Remember the two failure modes: a natural 1 on the pass is a **fumble** (the ball bounces and the drive is over), and any failed catch sends the ball scattering from the catcher's square - which is why the difference between 74% and 100% is exactly the part of the game that keeps you awake at night.
puzzles.author: demo

puzzles.title: Two Dice, and He Has Block
puzzles.imageAlt: Pitch diagram: blitzer making a two-dice blitz against the ball carrier
puzzles.task:
The opponent's ball carrier **#9** is standing in the middle of the pitch and your **Blitzer #2** can reach him with a Blitz. Declaring the Blitz gives you **two block dice and you may choose the better result**.

**#9 has Block**, so a Both Down result does *not* knock him over. You have **no Team Re-Roll** left this turn. All you need is for the carrier to go down - a Push is not enough.
puzzles.question: What is the chance that you knock the ball carrier down? (%)
puzzles.solution:
First work out how many of the 6 block dice faces actually knock the carrier down.

- **Skull** - your player goes down, the carrier is fine
- **Both Down** - against a defender with **Block** this is *not* a knockdown
- **Push** (2 faces) - no knockdown
- **Pow** (1 face) and **Pow/Push** (1 face) - knockdown

So 2 faces out of 6 succeed and 4 out of 6 fail.

**Two dice, choose the better one:** you fail only if *both* dice fail, so the chance to knock him down is 1 - (4/6)² = 1 - 16/36 = 20/36 = 5/9 = **55.56%**, i.e. **56%**.

Handy reference numbers for the same situation: 2 dice against a **Block** defender = 55.6%, 2 dice against a defender **without** Block = 75%, 1 die against a Block defender = 33.3%. That is the whole reason Block is the first skill on every shopping list.
puzzles.author: demo

puzzles.title: Two Rushes and a Prayer
puzzles.imageAlt: Pitch diagram: runner with the ball two squares short of the end zone
puzzles.task:
Your **#5 Runner** has the ball and is standing exactly 2 squares short of the end zone. His Movement is used up, so he has to make **two Rushes** (each is a **2+** roll) to get there. The ground is open and there is nothing else left to roll.

He has **Sure Feet**, which lets him **re-roll one failed Rush per turn**. No Team Re-Roll is left.
puzzles.question: What is the chance that he reaches the end zone? (%)
puzzles.solution:
A Rush is a 2+ roll: 5/6 = 83.33% per square.

**Case 1 - both Rushes succeed on the first try:** 5/6 x 5/6 = 25/36 = 69.44%.

**Case 2 - exactly one Rush fails, Sure Feet saves it:** the chance of exactly one failure is 2 x (1/6) x (5/6) = 10/36 = 27.78%; the re-roll then succeeds 5/6 of the time, so this case contributes 10/36 x 5/6 = 23.15%.

**Case 3 - both Rushes fail:** 1/36 = 2.78%, and it is a turnover.

Total: 69.44% + 23.15% = **92.59%**, so **93%**.

Useful sanity check: without Sure Feet the same run is only 25/36 = 69.4%. A single re-roll on a 5/6 roll is worth about 23 percentage points of touchdown.
puzzles.author: demo

puzzles.title: Two Dodges
puzzles.imageAlt: Pitch diagram: ball carrier dodging twice towards the end zone
puzzles.task:
Your ball carrier **#6** can only reach the end zone the painful way: the first Dodge goes into a square covered by one opponent (**4+**: AG 3+ with -1), and only then can he step into the end zone through a completely free square (**3+**). No Rushes are needed.

#6 has the **Dodge** skill, which may re-roll **one** failed Dodge per turn, and you have **no Team Re-Roll** left. You may of course choose when to spend the Dodge re-roll.
puzzles.question: Playing optimally, what is the chance you score the touchdown? (%)
puzzles.solution:
The interesting part is *when* you spend the once-per-turn Dodge re-roll. You need both rolls, so the re-roll has to go on the **first** roll - and the first roll is also the harder one, so it works out nicely.

- **Dodge 1 (4+ = 1/2)** with the Dodge re-roll available: 1 - (1/2)² = 3/4 = 75%
- **Dodge 2 (3+ = 2/3)** with no re-roll left: 2/3 = 66.67%

Total: 3/4 x 2/3 = **1/2 = 50%**.

For comparison, saving the re-roll for the second Dodge gives 1/2 x (1 - (1/3)²) = 1/2 x 8/9 = 44.4% - almost 6 percentage points worse. The lesson: spend a limited re-roll on your **hardest** roll first, never on the comfortable one you will probably pass anyway.
puzzles.author: demo

puzzles.title: The Long Bomb
puzzles.imageAlt: Pitch diagram: long pass across the pitch to a marked catcher in the end zone
puzzles.task:
Last turn of the match, 1-1 on the scoreboard. You need it all.

**#3 Thrower** is deep in your own half and has to fling the ball across the pitch: after all modifiers the pass needs a **5+** (2 faces out of 6). You have **one Team Re-Roll** left and it can be used on the pass roll (even if the thrower rolls a natural 1 fumble).

The pass is accurate, so the ball lands on **#4 Catcher** in the end zone. He is marked by one opponent, so after modifiers he catches on a **4+** (AG 3+ with -1). #4 has the **Catch** skill to re-roll a failed catch.
puzzles.question: What is the chance of the winning touchdown? (%)
puzzles.solution:
Two independent rolls, one re-roll for each.

**Pass (5+ with a Team Re-Roll):** a single try is 2/6 = 1/3 = 33.33%, so with the re-roll: 1 - (2/3)² = 5/9 = 55.56%.

**Catch (4+ with Catch):** a single try is 1/2 = 50%, so with the Catch re-roll: 1 - (1/2)² = 3/4 = 75%.

Total: 5/9 x 3/4 = 15/36 = 5/12 = **41.67%**, i.e. **42%**.

Two things worth internalising: the Team Re-Roll belongs on the pass because that is where it buys the most (6/9 - 3/9 = 33.3 percentage points, versus 25 points for the catch), and a 'long shot' turn like this still comes off better than one turn in three - long shots in Blood Bowl are rarely as hopeless as they feel.
